blocks.text: BC Assessment Farm Class (Class 9), ALC Rules & Floodplain Due Diligence

parts.t: Before purchasing farmland in Chilliwack, verify the parcel's zoning (such as AL Agricultural Lowland, AU Agricultural Upland, or R (Rural) zones under City of Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw No. 2020, No. 5000), confirm gross agricultural income thresholds required to maintain BC Assessment Farm Classification (Class 9) for reduced property taxes and GST/PTT treatment, inspect water licences and drainage ditches, and verify Flood Construction Levels under the City's Floodplain Regulation Bylaw.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Farms & Acreages Real Estate FAQs

parts.t: Where is agricultural farmland located in Chilliwack?

Chilliwack's primary ALR farmland districts are Greendale and Sumas Prairie on the west side, Yarrow and Majuba Hill in the southwest, East Chilliwack and Rosedale in the east, Fairfield Island along the Fraser River in the north, and Ryder Lake / Columbia Valley for upland hobby farms.
What is the difference between an acreage and a farm in Chilliwack?

In Fraser Valley real estate practice, properties between 1 and 10 acres are commonly referred to as rural acreages or hobby farms, while parcels of 10 acres or larger—or intensive commercial poultry, greenhouse, dairy, or nursery operations on 5+ acres—operate as full commercial farms.
How do you qualify for BC Assessment Farm Status (Class 9) in Chilliwack?

To qualify for BC Assessment Farm Classification (Class 9), a property must produce qualifying primary agricultural products for sale and meet annual gross farm income thresholds: $10,000 on parcels under 0.8 hectares (approx. 1.98 acres), $2,500 on parcels between 0.8 and 4 hectares (1.98 to 10 acres), and $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the farm land over 4 hectares.
Can you build a second house on ALR farmland in Chilliwack?

BC Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) regulations permit one principal residence plus one small additional residence (up to 90 sq m / 968 sq ft on parcels 40 ha or smaller, or up to 186 sq m on parcels over 40 ha) without an ALC non-adhering residential use application, provided the project also complies with City of Chilliwack zoning, septic/hydrogeological, and floodplain rules.
Is GST charged when buying a farm or acreage in Chilliwack?

GST treatment on farms and acreages depends on whether the land is used in a commercial farming business, whether a personal residence is included (which is generally apportioned out of commercial farm land), and whether the buyer is GST-registered. Always have your CPA and real estate lawyer structure the GST apportionment before subject removal.
Where can I find poultry farms with quota in Chilliwack?

Dedicated broiler, layer, breeder, and turkey farms in Chilliwack are listed on our Chilliwack Poultry Farms for Sale page. Quota may be included in the asking price or negotiated separately alongside the barns and land.
What water, drainage, and floodplain checks are needed on Chilliwack farms?

Buyers should verify provincial groundwater licences for irrigation or livestock wells, municipal drainage pump and ditch easements, manure storage compliance, soil capability classifications, and Fraser or Vedder River Flood Construction Levels.
